The use of bismuth citrate in a progressive hair-color cream for men's gray hair is permitted, limited to not more than 2.0 percent (w/v) of bismuth citrate in the cosmetic, and only for coloring hair on the scalp. The product may not be used on eyelashes, eyebrows, or body hair; it must not be applied to a cut or abraded scalp; and hands must be washed thoroughly after each use. The label must include the statement "Keep this product out of children's reach" and other warnings as specified. Certification for this color additive is exempt under the provisions of section 721(c) of the act, meaning no certification is required.

The amount of bismuth citrate in the cosmetic shall not be in excess of 2.0 percent (w/v) [5].  
The cosmetic may not be used for coloring eyelashes, eyebrows, or hair on parts of the body other than the scalp [6].  
The label of a cosmetic containing the color additive bismuth citrate shall bear, in addition to other information required by law, the following statement, conspicuously displayed thereon: "Keep this product out of children's reach. Do not use on cut or abraded scalp. Do not use to color eyelashes, eyebrows, or hair on parts of the body other than the scalp. Wash hands thoroughly after each use" [10].  
Certification of this color additive for the prescribed use is exempt from certification requirements under section 721(c) of the act [11].
